newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals calmer but still fragile.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals calmer but still fragile.

text.p: Southeast Asian currency markets were mostly calmer on Monday as players remained cautious after last week's moves by regional central banks to squeeze out speculators.
In Thailand, dealers said local banks continued to follow orders from the central bank not to sell dollars to offshore parties.
They said the Bank of Thailand (BOT)'s move was aimed at preventing offshore players from raising baht in the spot market to fund speculative positions.
The baht was quoted at 25.750/800 to the dollar at 0430 GMT against 25.775/25.875 late on Friday. The central bank fixed the mid-rate at 25.78 per dollar against 25.82 on Friday.
"On the spot market, we saw a lot of selling (of dollars) out of Bangkok from 25.90/26.00 down," a Singapore-based dealer said.
He said the baht was likely to stabilise around current levels. The BOT was not expected to take further action unless the baht weakened beyond 26.00 to the dollar again, he added.

The central bank made it clear on Friday that foreign speculators who sold the baht heavily for dollars would have to pay a high price to buy back baht from the more expensive swap market to square outstanding positions.

The baht/dollar one-month swap premium was trading at a high level of 30-55 satangs per dollar, unchanged from late on Friday. Before the attack on the baht last week, the swap premium averaged between 6.00-10.00 satangs per dollar.
In a daily market commentary, NatWest Markets recommended going long on the baht and adhering to the dollar/yen hedge to exploit its yield differential.
"However, to further protect out baht principal in case of another attack, players are urged to long the front end of the swap curve once another attack becomes imminent," it said.
In Indonesia, the rupiah came under pressure from concern over bouts of violence at the weekend in the build-up to the May 29 general election.
"The underlying tone is biddish on the dollar, reflecting the continuing violence in the election campaign," a Japanese bank dealer in Jakarta said.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,441.0/43.0 to the dollar at 0430 GMT, compared with Friday's 2,438.0/41.0.
On Saturday and Sunday, clashes between supporters of the ruling Golkar party and loyalists of the minority United Development Party (PPP) broke out in various parts of Jakarta.
Newspapers also said there was sporadic violence on Sunday in the ancient city of Yogyakarta and the nearby town of Bantul, but there were no injuries or arrests.
Jakarta'a police chief the situation was under control and witnesses said the capital was quiet on Monday.
Another Japanese bank dealer said the lower rupiah also resulted from short-covering by Singapore players ahead of a public holiday there on Wednesday and in Indonesia on Thursday.
"The market is quite active in the spot market. There are plenty of sellers and buyers," the dealer said.
Elsewhere, the Malaysian ringgit slipped as players covered their short dollar positions from last week but speculation about central bank support for the ringgit limited its downside, dealers said.

The ringgit had jumped sharply last week following a steep rise in tom/next rates on talk Bank Negara Malaysia had asked local banks to stop quoting tom/next rates to foreign parties, a move similar to what the Thai central bank did to squeeze out speculators.
Bank Negara denied it had issued instructions to local banks to stop undertaking swap transactions.
News of a huge trade surplus for March also helped the ringgit's rise last week but dealers said this had been largely priced in by Monday.
Dealers said tom/next rates had fallen back to more normal levels on Monday after trading as high as 300 on Friday.
The ringgit was quoted at 2.4927/37 to the dollar at 0430 GMT from its opening of 2.4850/60. It fell to a low of 2.4945/55 earlier.
A U.S. bank dealer in Singapore said the ringgit's downside was likely to be capped at 2.4950/2.5000 to the dollar on talk of central bank intervention.
"We saw a lot of Kuala Lumpur banks offering dollars around 2.4945/50 this morning so that's probably an indication that Negara might be around," he said.
-- Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Sonali Desai in Singapore.
